Here's the shift: you're not asking investors for checks — you're creating a marketplace they compete inside. Xavier's framing: "you are not raising. You're not trying to get someone to give you a check. You are creating a marketplace for as written." That changes our approach to running the bridge round (specific, time-bound, a start date and an end date), to investor conversations (momentum, not plea — "No, Hi, I am raising money. It is happening."), to advisor introductions (the Emery Park introduction held back until somebody is on the hook), to the YC application (committed, this week), and to the near-term priority (stop building, go sell).

Before — your own words on July 20: "I'm raising 500k at this point to do a bridge round to get me to enough enterprise traction that I can do a true, you know, million seed." As written, that's a request for runway: money now to buy the time to earn traction later, the seed a milestone out ahead.

Through the shift, the same line reads as the opening of a staged market: the paid enterprise pilot and everything already ingested are the goods on the table, the round runs between fixed dates so that maximal VCs compete, and the "million seed" stops being a milestone to beg toward — it's what happens when the market clears. YC is one venue inside that process, not a separate plea.
